Read source Proposition 3.2 and its counting proof, Proposition 3.14 and its induced-component proof, and Theorem 3.15 and its full transversal-lifting proof. This route is excluded as a routine direct source-formula argument. Set L=HN. Every H-double coset HgH maps into LgL, and its parameter t=[H:H intersect H^g] is at least T=[L:L intersect L^g]: because N lies in L intersect L^g and L=HN, T=[H:H intersect L^g]. Every L-double coset has at least one H-double coset above it. Since 0<f(t)<=1 and f decreases, multiplying within each coarse double coset gives product f(t)<=f(T). Multiply over the coarse double cosets. This supplies the asked inequality directly, but not a substantive campaign nomination. Equality characterization was not pursued.

For a finite group X and subgroups Y,Z, form a simple bipartite incidence graph with disjoint vertex parts {Yx:x∈X} and {Zx:x∈X}, with an edge joining Yx and Zx for each x∈X (duplicate edges identified). Right multiplication by X is edge-transitive. A vertex Yx has degree [Y:Y∩Z], and a vertex Zx degree [Z:Y∩Z]: at the identity coset its incident edges correspond to elements of Y, with equal opposite cosets precisely when their representatives differ by an element of Y∩Z. Thus the graph is regular exactly when |Y|=|Z|, and then the two parts have equal sizes. Connectivity is equivalent to ⟨Y,Z⟩=X: paths starting at the identity edge reach precisely the cosets with representatives in that subgroup. The kernel of the diagonal action is core_X(Y)∩core_X(Z), so this intersection being trivial makes the action faithful.

The complete applicable public argument is: with K=pG≅C_n and quotient C_p², the greedy quotient-line procedure of Lemma 3.3 finds k=n−|S_K| disjoint blocks T_i of length≤p, with nonzero sums in K, leaving R whose subset sums hit all K-cosets, provided |S|≥pn+2p²−p−1. The proof first gets a nonzero K-sum from 2p−1 terms in one line: two distinct subset sums have the same quotient image, and another p−1 terms cancel their image; factoring quotient-zero blocks gives one of length≤p with nonzero actual sum. The greedy length reserve ensures this at every step. If the leftover quotient sum is proper, it concentrates all but p−2 terms in one line. Backward maximal-line choice then forces every extracted block into that same line, contradicting regularity in its inverse image.

8. **Monomial immanant positivity — hooks publicly settled, full problem too broad.** McNulty, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39021v1,28Oct2026, actual Conjectures1.1/1.2 quote Stembridge/Haiman: for every partition lambda and totally nonnegative matrix, monomial immanant >=0; stronger at q=1 every monomial virtual character is nonnegative on every KL basis element. Original historical papers unread, attribution bounded. Actual Theorem1.3 proves all hook shapes; Theorem3.1 is the complementary-submatrix product positivity theorem and Section4's proof reduces marked-cycle functions through parabolic cosets and nonnegative localization multiplicities (proof end was read). History: no hook/immanant match in reports. Mechanism: character expansion and hyperbolic-localization products. Decisive next calculation would be an actual nonhook coefficient outside the paper's generated positive semiring, then an all-shape bridge or literal counterexample. General Haiman/Stembridge is a familiar hard problem, so **defer hard**, not sustained target and not two separately counted families.

|Kelley, 1602.00208v3 (2016), Conj3.2: a universal γ>0 bounds |F1(p,t,r)|/|F1(p,t)| by (1/r!)^γ for every prime p and natural t,r; F1 consists of deg<p−1 polynomials vanishing on no nontrivial multiplicative coset.|**Park.** Thm2.2 proof reduces modulo x^k−β and requires repeated exponent residues for a vanished coset; Thm2.3 proves the weaker root bound2(p−1)^(1−1/(t−1))C^(1/(t−1)). Thm3.3's actual counting/Stirling proof derives O(t log p) only assuming Conj3.2. Removing large cosets does not supply independence of remaining root constraints. A new factorial-moment bound uniform in exponents is required; isolated prime enumeration cannot prove it.|

Pairwise disjoint cosets must transfer to pairwise disjoint integer residue classes. TheoremB handles n<=4 and TheoremA handles HSC for group order<1440, using gcd/index exclusions. **Reject famous-hard disguise:** the unrestricted implication would settle Herzog–Schönheim; no new harmonic-transfer mechanism. Bounded group enumeration cannot prove it. A semantic Herzog hit in r172 reinforces nonfreshness; no reattack.
